name: Business Communication
certifications: No formal certification; assessed by a writing portfolio and recorded presentations
Optional: Cambridge English B2 Business Vantage or C1 Business Higher

beginner.summary: For graduates, new joiners and staff who write and speak at work in English every day. Covers plain business English, emails, chat messages, short reports, meeting notes, calls with colleagues and clients, short presentations and slides, customer replies, instructions and handovers, communicating across cultures and editing your own writing, practised with real workplace tasks and feedback.
prerequisites: Uses email and a chat tool such as Teams or Slack
Willing to share writing samples and be recorded for feedback
outcomes: Write clear emails, chat messages, updates and short reports
Run calls and meetings with clear notes and actions
Give a short, well-structured presentation with simple slides
Reply to customers and colleagues across cultures in a professional tone

days.topic: Business Communication Overview and Writing Baseline
subtopics: What business communication covers: writing, speaking and listening
Audience, purpose and channel for every message
The cost of unclear messages at work
Choosing between email, chat, call and meeting
How the course works: real tasks, feedback and rewrites
Writing baseline: one email and one short update
Speaking baseline: a two-minute recorded introduction
Reading feedback and choosing what to fix first
Personal goals and a writing log
days.lab_task: Write a real work email and a short status update, record a two-minute introduction to your role, score both against the course rubric with a partner and set three goals.
days.deliverable: Baseline email, update, recording and three goals
checks: Each piece has rubric scores for clarity, tone and structure
Correct channel chosen for five sample situations with a reason
Three specific goals linked to rubric scores

days.topic: Plain English for Business: Short Sentences and Everyday Words
subtopics: Why plain English is faster to read
Short words in place of long ones
Jargon, acronyms and when to explain them
Numbers, dates and units written clearly
days.lab_task: Rewrite three dense paragraphs from real policies or emails into plain English, cut each by at least a third without losing meaning and compare readability scores before and after.
days.deliverable: Three rewritten paragraphs with before-and-after scores
checks: Each rewrite is at least a third shorter
A partner finds no lost facts in the rewrites
Readability score improves for every paragraph

days.topic: Writing Clear Business Emails: Subject Lines, Structure and Calls to Action
subtopics: Subject lines that say what the email is about
Putting the main point or request first
Clear requests with owners and dates
To, Cc and Bcc used correctly
Attachments and links that readers can open
days.lab_task: Rewrite four real emails so the request is in the first two lines, add specific subject lines and deadlines, fix recipients and attachments, and test them on a partner who must state the request after ten seconds of reading.
days.deliverable: Four rewritten emails with a sending checklist
checks: A partner names the request after ten seconds of reading
Every subject line names the topic and any action
Every request names who acts and by when

days.topic: Email Tone, Etiquette and Replying to Difficult Messages
subtopics: How tone is read when there is no voice
Words that sound rude or passive-aggressive
Replying to complaints and criticism calmly
Saying no and pushing back politely
When to stop emailing and call
Waiting before sending an emotional reply
days.lab_task: Reply to three difficult emails (an angry client, a blaming colleague and an unrealistic deadline), have a partner rate the tone of each reply and revise any reply rated defensive or vague.
days.deliverable: Three replies with tone ratings and revisions
checks: Every reply is rated calm and professional by a partner
The deadline reply declines and offers an alternative
No reply forwards or exposes confidential content

days.topic: Chat and Instant Messaging at Work: Teams and Slack Etiquette
subtopics: When chat suits better than email
Writing complete messages instead of just "hi"
Emojis, reactions and tone in chat
Sharing files and decisions so they can be found
Moving a chat to a call or meeting
Chat messages that need a written record
days.lab_task: Turn a messy team chat about a production issue into a clean thread with one complete opening message, a clear owner, a summary of the decision and a link to the record, and agree response-time norms for the team.
days.deliverable: Rewritten thread, decision summary and team chat norms
checks: The opening message has context, request and urgency
The decision is summarised and linked from the thread
Team norms state response times and channel use

days.topic: Grammar and Punctuation That Readers Notice
subtopics: Tenses for past, present and planned work
Commas, full stops and run-on sentences
Apostrophes and common confusions such as its and it's
Capital letters, titles and product names
Common errors in Indian and international English
Using editor tools without trusting them blindly
days.lab_task: Find and fix the errors in ten workplace sentences and one full email, record your three most frequent errors in the writing log and correct them in your own baseline email.
days.deliverable: Corrected exercises, email and an updated writing log
checks: At least nine of ten sentences corrected
Three personal error patterns recorded with examples
Baseline email rewritten without those errors

days.topic: Writing Short Reports and Status Updates
subtopics: What readers want from a status update
Status in one line: on track, at risk or late
Progress, next steps, risks and help needed
Weekly updates that take two minutes to read
Keeping a consistent format each week
days.lab_task: Write a weekly status update for a real or sample project in one page, with a one-line status, progress, next steps, risks and help needed, then rewrite a two-page report into the same format.
days.deliverable: Two status updates in a reusable template
checks: The first line states status and the reason
Help needed names a person and a date
Each update fits on one page

days.topic: Meeting Communication: Agendas, Minutes and Action Items
subtopics: Deciding whether a meeting is needed
Invitations with purpose, agenda and pre-reading
Opening a meeting with the goal
Action items with owners and dates
days.lab_task: Plan a thirty-minute team meeting with an invitation and agenda, run it in class with role cards, take minutes and send them with action items within the session.
days.deliverable: Invitation, agenda, minutes and action list
checks: Purpose, agenda and expected outcome are stated
Every decision in the meeting appears in the minutes
Every action has one owner and a due date

days.topic: Speaking Clearly on Calls: Phone, Teams and Zoom
subtopics: Preparing for a call in two minutes
Opening with who you are and why you called
Pace, pauses and pronunciation for clarity
Following up a call in writing
days.lab_task: Make three recorded practice calls (a request to a colleague, a status call with a client and a call to clarify a requirement), review each recording against the checklist and send a follow-up email after each.
days.deliverable: Three call recordings, checklists and follow-up emails
checks: Each call states purpose in the first thirty seconds
Each call ends with a summary of agreed actions
Each follow-up email matches what was agreed

days.topic: Listening and Paraphrasing in Business Conversations
subtopics: Listening for facts, feelings and requests
Confirming requirements back to the speaker
days.lab_task: In pairs, listen to a colleague describe a work problem for five minutes, paraphrase it back, ask three clarifying questions and write a five-line summary the speaker agrees is accurate.
days.deliverable: Paraphrase recording and an agreed summary
checks: The speaker confirms the paraphrase without corrections
At least two open clarifying questions are asked
The written summary is approved by the speaker

days.topic: Presenting a Short Update to Your Team
subtopics: A simple structure: point, reason, example, point
Speaking from notes, not reading slides
days.lab_task: Prepare and deliver a three-minute update on your work with one main message, record it, watch it back with a partner and deliver an improved version.
days.deliverable: Two recordings with feedback notes
checks: The audience can repeat the main message
The talk finishes within three minutes and fifteen seconds
The second recording scores higher on the rubric

days.topic: Designing Simple Slides
subtopics: Turning a text-heavy deck into clear slides
days.lab_task: Redesign a ten-slide text-heavy deck so each slide has a headline that states the point, no more than thirty words and one visual, and run the accessibility checker on the result.
days.deliverable: Redesigned deck with before-and-after comparison
checks: Every slide headline states a point, not a topic
No slide has more than thirty words
The accessibility checker reports no errors
objectives: Use headlines that make a point

days.topic: Client Calls: Opening, Clarifying and Closing
subtopics: Preparing questions and the outcome you want
Handling a question you cannot answer
Writing the call summary for the client
days.lab_task: Run a role-played client call to clarify a new requirement, use a call plan, avoid committing to unconfirmed dates and send the client a summary that the role-play client confirms.
days.deliverable: Call plan, recording and client summary
checks: The call plan lists the goal and at least five questions
No date or scope is committed without confirmation
The client confirms the summary is accurate
objectives: Run client calls with a plan

days.topic: Writing for Customers: Responses, Apologies and Complaints
subtopics: What customers need in a reply
Explaining what happens next and when
Closing the loop after a fix
tools: Helpdesk tool such as Zendesk or ServiceNow
days.lab_task: Write replies to five customer complaints of different severity, including one escalation and one follow-up after a fix, and score them against a customer-reply rubric with a partner.
days.deliverable: Five customer replies with rubric scores
checks: Each reply names the customer's problem in the first lines
Each reply states what happens next and when
No reply reads as an unedited template in partner scoring

days.topic: Asking Questions and Requesting Information Politely
subtopics: Direct requests that are still courteous
Asking for clarification without sounding confused
Requests to senior people and other teams
Following up when there is no reply
days.lab_task: Write a set of requests for information to a peer, a senior manager and another team, plus a first and second follow-up, and compare responses to polite and blunt versions in a class exercise.
days.deliverable: Request set with follow-ups and a personal phrase bank
checks: Every request states what is needed and why
Follow-ups restate the request and add a date
Thank-you notes name what the person did

days.topic: Business Vocabulary and Common Phrases for Global Teams
subtopics: Everyday phrases for meetings and emails
Words for agreeing, disagreeing and suggesting
Phrases for deadlines, delays and priorities
False friends and local expressions to avoid
Numbers, currency and time zones in writing
days.lab_task: Replace local expressions and idioms in five sample messages with phrases that international colleagues understand, then use ten new phrases in a short meeting role play.
days.deliverable: Revised messages and a personal phrase bank of at least thirty phrases
checks: No confusing idioms remain in the revised messages
At least ten new phrases are used correctly in the role play
Dates, currencies and times are unambiguous for other regions

days.topic: Communicating Across Cultures and Time Zones
subtopics: Scheduling and writing across time zones
days.lab_task: Analyse a failed exchange between teams in India, Germany and the US, rewrite the key messages to suit each audience and write an asynchronous handover that works across time zones.
days.deliverable: Case analysis, rewritten messages and a handover note
checks: The analysis names the style differences that caused it
Each rewritten message suits its audience in peer review
The handover can be acted on without a call

days.topic: Giving Clear Instructions and Handovers
subtopics: Starting with the goal of the task
Handovers before leave or shift changes
days.lab_task: Write step-by-step instructions for a routine task in your job and a handover note for one week of leave, then have a partner follow the instructions without asking questions.
days.deliverable: Tested instructions and a handover note
checks: A partner completes the task using only the instructions
The instructions state what a correct result looks like
The handover lists open items, contacts and deadlines

days.topic: Proofreading and Editing Your Own Writing
subtopics: Editing in passes: structure, sentences, words
Proofreading on screen and on paper
days.lab_task: Edit a one-page document in three passes, record each change and its reason, then build a personal pre-send checklist from your writing log and use it on two new emails.
days.deliverable: Edited document, change log and a personal checklist
checks: The change log shows separate structure, sentence and word passes
All names, numbers and dates are verified
Both new emails pass the personal checklist

days.topic: Beginner Capstone: Business Communication Portfolio
days.lab_task: Build a portfolio from your own work: two emails, a chat thread, a status update, meeting minutes, a customer reply and a recorded three-minute presentation, then compare the rubric scores with your baseline.
days.deliverable: Communication portfolio with baseline comparison
checks: Every required piece is present and from real or realistic work
Rubric scores improve on the baseline for each skill
The presentation keeps to time with a clear main message
objectives: Apply beginner skills to real work
Communicate professionally in writing and speech

intermediate.summary: For professionals, team leads and client-facing staff who write for decision makers and present to groups. Covers structuring messages with the pyramid principle, executive summaries, proposals and business cases, persuasive presentations, data storytelling, handling questions, decision meetings, writing for senior stakeholders, negotiation language, bad news and escalations, client status reporting, process documents, explaining technical topics and writing feedback.
prerequisites: Has presented to a team or client at least a few times
Works with stakeholders in other teams or at clients
outcomes: Structure documents and talks so decision makers act on them
Write proposals, business cases and executive summaries
Present data and recommendations persuasively and handle tough questions
Communicate bad news, escalations and change requests professionally

days.topic: Structuring Messages with the Pyramid Principle
subtopics: Grouping ideas into three or four reasons
Applying the structure to emails and slides
days.lab_task: Restructure a chronological five-page report into a pyramid with the answer first and three grouped reasons, then turn it into a one-page email and a five-slide outline.
days.deliverable: Pyramid outline, one-page email and slide outline
checks: The first sentence states the recommendation
Supporting points are grouped and do not overlap
The slide outline follows the same pyramid

days.topic: Writing Executive Summaries
subtopics: The decision or ask in one sentence
Numbers that matter and those that do not
Risks and what is needed to proceed
Testing the summary on a busy reader
days.lab_task: Write a half-page executive summary for a long business document, test it on a partner playing a busy executive who has sixty seconds, and revise until they can state the ask and the recommendation.
days.deliverable: Tested executive summary
checks: The executive states the decision requested after sixty seconds
The summary fits within half a page
The summary includes cost, benefit and timing

days.topic: Business Proposals and Recommendations
subtopics: Options considered and why one is recommended
days.lab_task: Write a three-page proposal for a process improvement in your area, with options, a recommendation, cost and timeline, and have a review panel score it against a proposal rubric.
days.deliverable: Proposal with panel scores and revisions
checks: At least two options are compared with reasons
Cost and timeline are specific and justified
Panel scores meet the rubric threshold after revision

days.topic: Writing Business Cases for Approval
subtopics: The parts of a business case
days.lab_task: Build a business case for a tool or process investment with costs, benefits, payback and two what-if scenarios, write the one-page version and answer five questions from a role-played finance partner.
days.deliverable: Business case with a one-page summary and Q&A notes
checks: Costs, benefits and payback are calculated with stated assumptions
Two what-if scenarios show how results change
All five finance questions are answered from the case

days.topic: Persuasive Presentations: Structure and Evidence
subtopics: Knowing what the audience must believe and do
Emotional and logical appeal in balance
days.lab_task: Prepare and deliver a ten-minute persuasive presentation recommending a change at work, with evidence for each claim and a clear call to action, and collect audience votes before and after.
days.deliverable: Persuasive deck, recording and audience vote results
checks: Every main claim has evidence on the slide or in speech
The talk ends with a specific call to action
Audience support increases between the before and after votes
objectives: Close with a clear call to action

days.topic: Data Storytelling: Charts That Make the Point
subtopics: Starting from the question and the insight
Choosing the right chart for the comparison
days.lab_task: Turn a data table into a three-chart story with insight titles and highlighted points, present it in five minutes and check that the audience can state the insight from each chart.
days.deliverable: Three-chart story and presentation recording
checks: Each chart type suits its comparison
Every chart title states the insight in words
The audience states each insight correctly

days.topic: Handling Questions and Objections After a Presentation
subtopics: Saying "I don't know" and following up
Objections about cost, risk and timing
Bridging back to the main message
days.lab_task: Present a recommendation for five minutes and take ten minutes of prepared hard questions from the class, then review the recording for answer length, accuracy and bridges back to the message.
days.deliverable: Question bank and reviewed Q&A recording
checks: The question bank covers at least ten likely questions with answers
Most answers take under a minute
Hostile questions are answered without defensiveness

days.topic: Decision Meetings: Pre-Reads, Options and Decision Records
subtopics: Meetings that exist to make a decision
Framing options and criteria before the meeting
Communicating the decision to people who were absent
days.lab_task: Prepare a two-page pre-read with options and criteria, run a twenty-minute decision meeting with role cards, and publish a decision record and an announcement to the wider team.
days.deliverable: Pre-read, decision record and announcement
checks: The pre-read lists options with agreed criteria
The record states the decision, reasons and dissent
Absent people can act on the announcement alone

days.topic: Writing for Senior Stakeholders: Brevity and Decisions
subtopics: What senior stakeholders need from you
Asking for decisions with clear options
Updating on risks before they surprise
Tone with senior people: confident, not casual
Following up on senior requests quickly
days.lab_task: Write a three-line update, a one-page decision request and a risk warning to a senior stakeholder for the same situation, and have a role-played senior reviewer rate each for clarity and confidence.
days.deliverable: Three senior-facing messages with reviewer ratings
checks: Each message states the point in the first line
The decision request gives options with a recommendation
The risk warning states impact, likelihood and the proposed action

days.topic: Negotiation Language in Email and Meetings
subtopics: Preparing your position and walk-away point
Phrases for proposing and conditional offers
Saying no while keeping the relationship
Negotiating over email: risks and tactics
days.lab_task: Negotiate a scope and deadline change with a role-played client, using conditional offers and summaries, then send a confirmation email that both sides agree reflects the deal.
days.deliverable: Negotiation plan, recording and confirmation email
checks: The plan states goals, walk-away point and the other side's interests
At least two offers use "if you, then we" structure
Both sides agree the email reflects the deal

days.topic: Delivering Bad News and Escalations in Writing
subtopics: When bad news must be written and when spoken first
Stating the news clearly and early
What you are doing and what you need
Escalation paths and when to use them
Following up after the bad news
days.lab_task: Write a delay notice to a client, an internal escalation to your manager's manager and a follow-up update for the same incident, and have a partner check that each is factual and states actions.
days.deliverable: Delay notice, escalation and follow-up
checks: The bad news is in the first two sentences
No message blames individuals or speculates
Each message states actions and the next update time

days.topic: Client Communication: Status Reports, Steering Updates and Change Requests
subtopics: What clients expect in regular reporting
days.lab_task: Produce a weekly client status report, a five-slide steering update and a change request for a scope addition on a sample engagement, and present the steering update to a role-played client.
days.deliverable: Status report, steering deck and change request
checks: The status report shows status, progress, risks and asks
The change request states cost, time and risk impact
The client approves or rejects the change in the session

days.topic: Communicating in Virtual and Hybrid Teams
subtopics: Video meeting habits that include remote people
Hybrid meetings with people in a room
Written updates in place of status meetings
days.lab_task: Replace one recurring status meeting with a written asynchronous update for a week in a simulation, run one hybrid meeting with remote participants and write a team communication charter.
days.deliverable: Asynchronous update set, hybrid meeting notes and a charter
checks: Team members get the same information without the meeting
Remote participants speak as often as people in the room
The charter sets channels, response times and meeting rules

days.topic: Writing Policies, Procedures and Process Documents
subtopics: Reviewing documents with the people who use them
days.lab_task: Rewrite a confusing process document as a procedure with clear responsibilities, numbered steps and a swimlane diagram, and test it with two people who perform the process.
days.deliverable: Procedure with diagram and user test notes
checks: Every step has an owner role
The swimlane matches the written steps
Both users complete the process without questions

days.topic: Communicating Technical Topics to Non-Technical Audiences
subtopics: Finding what the audience cares about
Levels of detail for different readers
Turning a technical document into a briefing
days.lab_task: Explain a technical change such as a system migration to a role-played business audience in five minutes, then write a one-page briefing and check that the audience can explain the impact back.
days.deliverable: Briefing note and presentation recording
checks: The briefing has no unexplained technical terms
Impact is stated in cost, time, risk or customer terms
The audience explains the impact correctly

days.topic: Feedback in Writing: Reviews, Comments and Appraisal Notes
subtopics: Written feedback that helps rather than hurts
Comments on documents and code reviews
Responding to written feedback you receive
days.lab_task: Write review comments on a colleague's document, draft appraisal notes for a sample employee using behaviour and impact, and check both against a bias checklist.
days.deliverable: Document comments and appraisal notes with a bias check
checks: Every comment names behaviour and impact
No appraisal sentence fails the bias checklist
Appraisal notes include strengths and development areas with examples

days.topic: Webinars and Online Presentations
subtopics: Slides and visuals for small screens
Polls, chat and questions to involve people
days.lab_task: Plan and deliver a fifteen-minute webinar to the class with a producer, one poll and a live question session, then review the recording and the attendee feedback.
days.deliverable: Webinar plan, recording and feedback summary
checks: At least one poll and three audience questions are handled
A planned technical interruption is handled smoothly
Feedback scores and attendance are summarised with actions

days.topic: AI Writing Tools: Drafting, Checking and Disclosing
subtopics: Where AI writing assistants help and where they mislead
Prompting for drafts in your own voice
Checking facts, names and numbers in AI drafts
Editing AI text so it sounds human and specific
Using AI for summaries and translations
Building a personal AI writing checklist
days.lab_task: Use an AI assistant to draft a client update and a meeting summary, check every fact against the source, edit both into your own voice and record what was changed and why.
days.deliverable: AI-assisted drafts, edited versions and a change record
checks: Every fact in the final text matches the source
No confidential data is entered into unapproved tools
Reviewers cannot spot generic AI phrasing in the final versions

days.topic: Networking Conversations and Professional Profiles
subtopics: Starting and ending conversations at events
days.lab_task: Write a thirty-second introduction, rewrite your profile headline and summary, practise three networking conversations in class and send two follow-up messages that receive replies in the role play.
days.deliverable: Introduction, revised profile and follow-up messages
checks: The introduction states role, value and a hook in thirty seconds
The headline and summary state what you do and for whom
Follow-up messages are specific to the conversation

days.topic: Intermediate Capstone: Proposal, Presentation and Q&A for a Business Decision
days.lab_task: Take a real business decision from your work, write an executive summary and a proposal, present it for ten minutes to a role-played decision panel, handle their questions and publish the decision record and follow-up.
days.deliverable: Proposal pack, presentation recording and decision record
checks: Executive summary and proposal meet the rubric threshold
The panel reaches a decision in the session
Answers are brief, accurate and calm
objectives: Win a decision with writing and speaking

advanced.summary: For managers, senior leaders and communication leads who speak for a function or the organisation. Covers board papers and decision memos, strategic narratives, organisational change communication, crisis statements, media and spokesperson skills, announcements, internal communications, keynote speaking, complex negotiations, communicating risk, regulator and auditor communication, difficult all-hands messages, communication strategy and measurement, coaching others, style guides, inclusive global communication and ethical persuasion.
prerequisites: Leads a team, function or major client relationship
Writes for and presents to senior leaders regularly
Has completed intermediate business communication or has equivalent experience
outcomes: Write board-level papers and strategy narratives that drive decisions
Plan and run communication for change, crises and difficult announcements
Represent the organisation to media, regulators, investors and large audiences
Build communication strategies, style guides and capability in others

days.topic: Executive Communication: Board Papers and Decision Memos
subtopics: What a board or executive committee needs from a paper
Paper structure: purpose, recommendation, rationale, risks
Pre-wiring key members before the meeting
Presenting a paper in five minutes
Common reasons papers are sent back
days.lab_task: Write a board paper and a two-page decision memo for a significant investment, pre-wire two role-played board members, and present the paper in five minutes to a mock board that votes.
days.deliverable: Board paper, decision memo and mock board outcome
checks: The recommendation and decision required are on page one
Key risks have mitigations and owners
The mock board approves or gives specific conditions

days.topic: Strategic Narrative: Communicating Strategy and Direction
subtopics: The strategic narrative: where we are, where we are going, why, how
Turning strategy documents into a story
Messages for different levels of the organisation
Checking that people can explain the strategy
days.lab_task: Turn a ten-page strategy document into a one-page narrative and a five-minute talk, write a manager cascade kit and test whether a sample audience can explain the strategy in their own words.
days.deliverable: Strategic narrative, talk and cascade kit
checks: The narrative covers where, why and how in one page
The cascade kit includes key messages, questions and answers
Most of the sample audience explains the strategy correctly

days.topic: Change Communication Plans for Organisations
subtopics: Stakeholder impact analysis for a change
Sequencing who hears what and when
Key messages, FAQs and manager briefings
Adjusting the plan as the change progresses
days.lab_task: Build a communication plan for a system or process change affecting three departments, with a stakeholder impact map, sequenced messages, FAQs, a manager briefing and measures, and present it to a role-played change board.
days.deliverable: Change communication plan with supporting materials
checks: Every stakeholder group has an impact rating and needs
Leaders and managers hear before staff and customers
The plan defines understanding and adoption measures with targets

days.topic: Crisis Communication: Statements, Holding Lines and Updates
subtopics: Types of crises and their communication needs
Facts, empathy and action in every message
Internal, customer, partner and public audiences
days.lab_task: Run a timed crisis simulation for a data breach, issue a holding statement within twenty minutes, then customer, staff and public updates as new facts arrive, and review the communication afterwards.
days.deliverable: Crisis statements, update log and review
checks: The holding statement is approved within twenty minutes
No statement contains facts later shown to be wrong
Each update states impact, care and next steps

days.topic: Media and Spokesperson Skills
subtopics: How journalists work and what they need
Interview formats: live, recorded, print and podcast
Body language and voice on camera
Off the record and other risky ideas
days.lab_task: Prepare key messages for an announcement and take part in a recorded mock television interview and a hostile print interview, then review how often you delivered your key messages.
days.deliverable: Media briefing pack and interview recordings with review
checks: Three key messages with proof points are written
Each key message is delivered at least once per interview
Difficult questions are bridged back to messages without evasion

days.topic: Writing Announcements and Press Releases
subtopics: Press release structure and the inverted pyramid
Writing for search and social media
days.lab_task: Write a press release, a customer email and a staff announcement for the same product launch, coordinate their timing in a launch-day schedule and have a role-played journalist critique the release.
days.deliverable: Announcement set and launch-day schedule
checks: The first paragraph answers who, what, when and why
Staff hear before the public release goes out
The journalist would use the release with minor edits

days.topic: Internal Communications: Town Halls, Newsletters and Intranet
tools: Microsoft Teams Live Events or Zoom
days.lab_task: Plan and run a mock thirty-minute town hall with a leader message, live questions and a follow-up newsletter, and design a measure of reach for staff without desks.
days.deliverable: Town hall plan, newsletter and reach measures
checks: The agenda includes leader message, questions and actions
The plan reaches staff without email access
Reach and engagement measures are defined with a baseline

days.topic: Keynote and Conference Speaking
subtopics: Choosing a talk that fits the event
Structure for twenty to forty minutes
days.lab_task: Write and rehearse a twenty-minute conference talk, deliver it on a stage or large room setup with recording, get structured feedback and write a conference speaking proposal for the same talk.
days.deliverable: Talk recording, feedback and speaking proposal
checks: The talk has a clear opening, three ideas and a close
The talk ends within one minute of the planned time
The proposal includes title, abstract and audience takeaways

days.topic: Communication in Complex Negotiations
subtopics: Building a negotiation team and roles
Deadlock and how to break it
days.lab_task: Negotiate a three-party contract renewal with multiple issues in teams, trade across issues to reach agreement and write the heads of terms that all parties sign off.
days.deliverable: Negotiation plan, outcome and signed heads of terms
checks: The plan lists each party's interests and alternatives
The agreement includes at least two cross-issue trades
All parties approve the heads of terms

days.topic: Communicating Risk and Uncertainty
subtopics: Avoiding false precision and false comfort
Risk messages for boards, staff and customers
days.lab_task: Rewrite a risk report for a board and for staff using ranges, scenarios and plain frequencies, and test whether readers correctly interpret the likelihood and impact.
days.deliverable: Two risk communications with reader test results
checks: Probabilities are expressed as frequencies or ranges
Best, likely and worst cases are described
Most readers interpret likelihood and impact correctly

days.topic: Communicating with Regulators and Auditors
subtopics: Building a long-term relationship of trust
days.lab_task: Respond in writing to a role-played regulator's information request about an incident, prepare for and run a meeting with them, and log every commitment made with owners and dates.
days.deliverable: Written response, meeting notes and commitments log
checks: Every question in the request is answered or explained
All statements are supported by documents
Every commitment has an owner and a date

days.topic: Leading Difficult All-Hands Conversations: Layoffs, Reorganisations and Cost Cuts
subtopics: Legal and HR constraints on what can be said
The leader's message: decision, reasons, support
days.lab_task: Plan and deliver a role-played announcement of a reorganisation, including the sequence of conversations, the leader's script, a manager briefing and FAQs, then answer hard questions from the class.
days.deliverable: Announcement plan, script, briefing pack and FAQs
checks: Affected people are told before the wider announcement
Answers do not promise what cannot be guaranteed
The briefing pack covers questions managers will face

days.topic: Building a Communication Strategy for a Function
subtopics: Communication goals linked to business goals
days.lab_task: Audit the current channels of a function, write a one-year communication strategy with goals, audiences, channel mix, calendar and measures, and present it to a role-played leadership team.
days.deliverable: Channel audit and communication strategy
checks: Every communication goal supports a stated business goal
The calendar covers recurring and planned communication for a year
Roles and approval steps are defined

days.topic: Measuring Communication: Surveys, Analytics and Feedback Loops
subtopics: What to measure: reach, understanding, belief, action
days.lab_task: Design a measurement framework for a change campaign with reach, understanding and action measures, analyse sample survey and analytics data, and present three improvements to leadership.
days.deliverable: Measurement framework, analysis and improvement plan
checks: Measures cover reach, understanding and action
The analysis identifies at least two gaps from the data
Each improvement is linked to a measured gap

days.topic: Coaching Others to Write and Present Better
subtopics: Feedback that people can act on
Editing someone else's work without rewriting it
Peer review habits in a team
days.lab_task: Coach a colleague on a document and a presentation over two rounds, using questions and specific feedback, and measure the improvement with the rubric.
days.deliverable: Coaching notes and before-and-after rubric scores
checks: The top two problems are identified with examples
The colleague makes the changes themselves
Rubric scores improve after two rounds

days.topic: Brand Voice and Style Guides
subtopics: Templates and examples in the guide
Rolling out and maintaining the guide
days.lab_task: Write a style guide for a team with voice attributes, tone examples, terminology and formatting rules, then rewrite three existing pieces to follow it and collect feedback from writers.
days.deliverable: Style guide and three rewritten examples
checks: Each voice attribute has do and don't examples
The three rewrites follow every rule in the guide
Writers rate the guide as usable

days.topic: Inclusive Language, Translation and Localisation
subtopics: Inclusive language and why it matters
Accessibility: plain language, alt text and captions
Localisation of examples, dates and formats
days.lab_task: Revise a global announcement for inclusive language and translation readiness, translate it with a machine translation tool, have a native speaker review it and fix the problems found.
days.deliverable: Revised announcement, translation and review notes
checks: The revision passes the inclusive language checklist
Idioms and ambiguous phrases are removed
A native speaker confirms the translated meaning

days.topic: Ethical Persuasion and Building Trust
days.lab_task: Analyse two real communication cases where trust was lost, rewrite the key messages ethically, and write your own communication principles with examples of applying them.
days.deliverable: Case analyses, rewrites and personal principles
checks: Each analysis names the trust-breaking behaviour
Rewrites are honest about uncertainty and limits
Principles include examples from your own work

days.topic: Leading Communication Through Mergers and Acquisitions
subtopics: Day one messages for both organisations
days.lab_task: Plan communication for a role-played acquisition from announcement to the first ninety days, including day one messages for both workforces, customer letters and a manager toolkit.
days.deliverable: Ninety-day integration communication plan with materials
checks: The plan covers announcement, day one and ninety days
Day one messages speak to each organisation's concerns
The plan includes surveys or listening sessions with actions

days.topic: Advanced Capstone: Communication Plan for a Major Organisational Change
days.lab_task: Lead the communication for a major change in a realistic case: write the narrative, the sequenced plan with key materials, a difficult question pack and measures, and present the plan to a mock executive committee.
days.deliverable: Complete communication plan, materials and executive presentation
checks: The plan covers all stakeholders with sequence and channels
The question pack covers the hardest likely questions
The mock executive committee approves the plan
